restatements.text: Allows individuals who are 21 or older and legally permitted to possess a handgun to carry it concealed without needing a permit.
Directs sheriffs to keep issuing concealed carry permits to eligible applicants who request them for out-of-state reciprocity.

analysis.answer: Currently, individuals must complete an eight-hour safety course and obtain a permit from the county sheriff to carry a concealed handgun. This measure eliminates those requirements for anyone 21 or older who is lawfully allowed to possess a handgun.

Without the time and financial costs of applying for a permit and taking a mandatory safety course, more lawful gun owners are likely to carry concealed firearms. Local sheriffs' offices will process significantly fewer permit applications.

The measure addresses the entry barriers—costs, paperwork, and training mandates—associated with exercising the right to carry a concealed firearm. It removes the state's regulatory hurdle for lawful gun owners.

The effect of permitless concealed carry laws on public safety is highly disputed. Some researchers find that removing permit and training requirements leads to increases in violent crime and firearm homicides, while other studies conclude it has no significant impact on crime rates or may deter crime by increasing the number of armed, law-abiding citizens.

Because other states often require a permit for concealed carry reciprocity, individuals who travel frequently will continue applying for permits, maintaining a partial demand for the sheriff's licensing services.
